name: Emergency Water Storage
tagline: Vessel sanitization, chemical preservation, hydraulic isolation, and ration budgeting for prolonged survival and collapse recovery
problem:
When municipal water distribution networks fail, water pressure drops to zero within minutes. This pressure collapse causes back-siphonage: surrounding groundwater, chemical runoff, and raw sewer seepage are sucked through cracks in underground piping directly into the dry supply mains. Relying on tap lines during or immediately following a disruption guarantees ingestion of lethal pathogen loads.

Storing untreated water or using contaminated containers causes rapid biological explosion. A clean-looking container holding untreated surface water can develop tens of millions of colony-forming units (CFU) of enteric bacteria, Giardia cysts, and cyanobacteria within 72 hours at ambient room temperature. Furthermore, using improvised containers previously used for motor oil, agricultural pesticides, or industrial solvents leaches endocrine-disrupting chemicals and organophosphates that cannot be removed by boiling or simple filtration.

In long-duration space settlement or planetary habitats, water storage is not passive; it is the thermal mass and life-support buffer of the vessel. In zero-gravity or low-gravity environments, biofilms form exponentially faster along interior vessel walls due to lack of shear currents, creating biocidal resistance and clogging life-support recycling membranes.
overview:
Safe emergency water storage is governed by five interdependent engineering controls: Vessel Qualification, Shock Sanitization, Residual Chemical Preservation, Hydraulic Isolation, and Environmental Exclusion.

1. Vessel Qualification: Storage vessels must be chemically inert, impermeable to light, and food-grade certified (High-Density Polyethylene [HDPE, resin code 2], Polypropylene [PP, resin code 5], borosilicate glass, or 316-grade stainless steel). Non-food plastics leach toxic plasticizers, lead stabilizers, and antimony trioxide into stored water over time.

2. Shock Sanitization: Prior to filling, the container must undergo a chlorine shock rinse (15 mL of 5-6% sodium hypochlorite per 4 liters of water, creating a ~200 ppm solution) swirled across all interior surfaces, valve threads, and caps for at least 3 minutes, then drained.

3. Residual Preservation: Water is stabilized using regular, unscented household bleach (5-6% sodium hypochlorite) or calcium hypochlorite (HTH). Clear water requires 2 drops (0.1 mL) per liter (approx. 8 drops or 0.5 mL per gallon / 2 teaspoons per 55-gallon drum) to achieve a free available chlorine residual of 0.2 to 0.5 mg/L after a 30-minute contact dwell. If water is turbid, filtration through cloth or sand and doubling the dose is mandatory.

4. Hydraulic Isolation: The primary mechanism of post-treatment contamination is 'dipping'—using hands, cups, or unsterilized ladles to scoop water. Vessels must remain hermetically sealed, dispensing exclusively through a dedicated, food-grade bottom tap or clean manual siphon valve with a downward spout.

5. Storage Environment: Containers must be elevated at least 15 cm off concrete floors on wooden or plastic dunnage pallets. Concrete is porous and off-gases volatile petrochemical vapors that migrate through polyethylene over months. Water must be stored in total darkness below 20°C to prevent photochemical breakdown of chlorine and cyanobacterial blooms, with full stock rotation every 6 to 12 months.

principles.name: The Closed Hydraulic Standard (Anti-Dipping)
principles.explanation: Dipping hands, cups, or ladles into stored drinking water causes over 80% of secondary bacteriological outbreaks in humanitarian crises. A strict closed design with narrow threaded bungs and downward spigots prevents hands and airborne dust from contacting the bulk fluid.

principles.name: Free Available Chlorine Residual (FAC)
principles.explanation: Disinfection is a dynamic chemical equilibrium. Achieving an initial kill is insufficient; maintaining a free chlorine residual of 0.2 to 0.5 mg/L ensures that any rogue bacterial spores or airborne pathogens entering during liquid drawdown are immediately neutralized.

principles.name: Polymer Integrity and Osmotic Migration
principles.explanation: Polyethylene polymers (HDPE #2) are semi-permeable membranes on a molecular level over long storage windows. Volatile organic compounds (fuels, solvents, pesticide vapors) from bare concrete floors or shared garage storage can migrate across drum walls into water. Elevation on dunnage is mandatory.

principles.name: Thermal and Photonic Retardation
principles.explanation: Sunlight (photons) accelerates the photolysis of free hypochlorite into inactive chloride and chlorate ions, while providing photosynthetic energy for algae. Complete light exclusion and storage below 20°C preserves chemical stability and prevents biological regrowth.

principles.name: Survival Water Rationing Geometry
principles.explanation: Baseline physiological survival requires 3 to 5 liters of potable water per person per day for drinking and minimal food rehydration. Comprehensive survival hygiene, sanitation, and medical washing requires a minimum of 15 to 20 liters per person per day.

components.name: Food-Grade HDPE Storage Drum / Carboy
components.function: Hermetically contains the water volume without leaching toxins or allowing light penetration
components.position: Central storage unit elevated on pallet
components.madeFrom: High-Density Polyethylene (HDPE #2) with opaque blue/black UV-inhibiting pigmentation
components.criticalNote: Verify the embossed 'fork and cup' symbol or resin ID #2. Never repurpose oil, chemical, or dye barrels.

components.name: Food-Grade Dispensing Tap / Siphon Valve
components.function: Allows controlled liquid dispensing without opening top access bungs or introducing dipped utensils
components.position: Threaded into the lower 3/4-inch bung or top siphon entry port
components.madeFrom: Food-grade Polypropylene (PP) or lead-free 304/316 stainless steel with PTFE seal tape
components.criticalNote: Disinfect the spigot outlet before each major drawdown with 70% alcohol or boiling water.

components.name: Bung Plugs with Silicone Gaskets
components.function: Provides an airtight, watertight mechanical seal preventing atmospheric contamination and vapor loss
components.madeFrom: EPDM or food-grade silicone O-rings with threaded HDPE plugs
components.criticalNote: Replace cracked gaskets annually; dry rot creates an invisible entry vector for fruit flies and mold.

components.name: Air Relief Vent with Micron Filter
components.function: Allows smooth liquid discharge without hydraulic vacuum lock while filtering incoming replacement air
components.position: Upper drum bung or vent cap
components.madeFrom: Hydrophobic PTFE 0.2-micron air filter membrane in polypropylene housing
components.criticalNote: Never vent directly to open air; airborne fungal spores and dust mites will colonize the damp headspace.

components.name: Storage Elevation Dunnage / Pallet
components.function: Physically decouples drum base from concrete floors, preventing chemical vapor migration and moisture rot
components.madeFrom: Hardwood timber pallets, plastic grids, or structural masonry blocks
components.criticalNote: Ensure level, stable load bearing: a 55-gallon drum weighs ~210 kg (460 lbs) when full.

components.name: Chlorine Dosing Dropper & Test Kit
components.function: Delivers measured biocide volumes and verifies residual free chlorine levels
components.position: Stored in water test cabinet adjacent to drums
components.madeFrom: Amber glass eyedropper (calibrated to 20 drops/mL) and DPD-1 colorimetric chlorine test strips
components.criticalNote: Bleach degrades over time; unopened bleach loses ~20% potency every 6 months at room temperature.

rawMaterials.name: Potable Feedwater
rawMaterials.purpose: Primary hydration and medical life support fluid
earthLocations: Municipal treated supply, protected deep artesian wells, or properly clarified and filtered surface water
rawMaterials.spaceAlternatives: Catalytically oxidized and polished urine/condensate distillate from ECLSS water recovery loops
rawMaterials.processingRequired: Pre-filter through 5-micron sediment filter if turbidity exceeds 1 NTU prior to chlorination.

rawMaterials.name: Sodium Hypochlorite (5-6% Bleach) or Calcium Hypochlorite (HTH 65%)
rawMaterials.purpose: Residual biocide destroying bacteria, viruses, and inhibiting algae/biofilm proliferation
earthLocations: Household grocery stock, water treatment supply depots, swimming pool chemical stores
rawMaterials.spaceAlternatives: Electrolytically generated chlorine from brine electrolysis cells or silver/copper ion biocide generators
rawMaterials.processingRequired: Inspect for purity: must contain zero fragrances, zero surfactants, and zero heavy metal thickeners.

rawMaterials.name: High-Density Polyethylene (HDPE Resin)
rawMaterials.purpose: Structural polymer for barrels, bungs, and dispensing fittings
earthLocations: Industrial container manufacturers, food processing plants, agricultural supply centers
rawMaterials.spaceAlternatives: Rotomolded polyethylene synthesized from Sabatier ethylene feeds or sintered aluminium pressure carboys
rawMaterials.processingRequired: Wash with alkaline detergent and rinse with 200 ppm chlorine solution before filling.

rawMaterials.name: Food-Grade Silicone / EPDM Elastomer
rawMaterials.purpose: Resilient gasket seals for bungs and spigot threads
earthLocations: Plumbing supply houses, brewing supply stores, gasket fabricators
rawMaterials.spaceAlternatives: Fluoropolymer (PTFE) O-rings or metal C-ring compression seals
rawMaterials.processingRequired: Sterilize in boiling water or wipe with 70% isopropyl alcohol.

rawMaterials.name: Structural Timber or Plastic Pallets
rawMaterials.purpose: Physical elevation dunnage to eliminate vapor migration from flooring
earthLocations: Shipping yards, hardware warehouses, construction scrap timber
rawMaterials.spaceAlternatives: Extruded aluminium strut framing anchored to bulkhead tie-downs
rawMaterials.processingRequired: Ensure surface is free of nails or splinters that could puncture polymer drum walls.

buildSteps.title: Vessel Inspection and Food-Grade Validation
buildSteps.description: Inspect drum or carboy interior with an LED flashlight for cracks, chemical odors, or residue. Confirm the embossed triangular recycle code #2 (HDPE) or #5 (PP) and the food-safe cup-and-fork logo. Reject any container with unknown provenance or petrochemical smell.
buildSteps.warningNote: Never use plastic trash cans or pickle barrels; trash cans contain toxic mold inhibitors, and pickle plastic absorbs vinegar aromatics that accelerate chemical leaching.

buildSteps.title: Shock Sanitization Wash
buildSteps.description: Prepare a 200 ppm sanitizing solution by mixing 15 mL (1 tablespoon) of unscented 5-6% household bleach per 4 liters of clean water. Pour into the vessel, seal tightly, and roll/tilt the drum so all internal surfaces, bungs, and valve threads are wetted for at least 3 minutes. Drain completely without rinsing.
buildSteps.warningNote: Wear safety goggles and nitrile gloves; splashing 200 ppm chlorine into eyes causes acute corneal irritation.

buildSteps.title: Feedwater Filtration and Filling
buildSteps.description: Connect a dedicated, food-grade drinking water hose (white RV grade) to the water source. If filling from surface water or wells, pass water through a 5-micron sediment filter or multi-layer sand filter. Fill the container to within 5 cm of the bung neck, leaving minimal air headspace.
buildSteps.warningNote: Standard garden hoses contain lead, plasticizers, and vinyl stabilizers that impart toxic chemical taints to stored water.

buildSteps.title: Chemical Preservation Dosing
buildSteps.description: Add 2 drops of fresh, unscented household bleach (5-6% sodium hypochlorite) per liter of water (approx. 2.5 teaspoons / 12.5 mL per 55-gallon drum). For calcium hypochlorite granules (HTH 65%), dissolve 1 level teaspoon in 1 liter of water to create stock, then add 50 mL of stock per 50 liters. Tightly seal bungs and rock the drum to mix.
buildSteps.warningNote: Do NOT use splash-less, scented, or color-safe bleaches. They contain sodium hydroxide thickeners and fragrances toxic for internal consumption.

buildSteps.title: Residual Verification Dwell Test
buildSteps.description: Allow the sealed container to dwell undisturbed for 30 minutes. Unseal the vent bung and test water with a DPD-1 colorimetric test strip or test kit. The free available chlorine must register between 0.2 and 0.5 mg/L, with a distinct faint chlorine smell. If no chlorine is detected, repeat dosing and dwell for another 15 minutes.
buildSteps.warningNote: If water smells strongly pungent or bleach burns the tongue, chlorine concentration is excessive; aerate or dilute with sterile water before drinking.

buildSteps.title: Spigot Installation and Hermetic Sealing
buildSteps.description: Wrap male spigot threads with 4 layers of virgin PTFE thread seal tape. Thread the spigot into the 3/4-inch bung opening until torque is firm and gasket is compressed. Tighten the 2-inch main bung with an aluminium drum wrench to approx. 25-30 Nm torque.
buildSteps.warningNote: Do not overtighten poly fittings; stripped threads cause catastrophic slow leaks that ruin floorboards and drain water reserves.

buildSteps.title: Elevation, Siting, and Rotation Maintenance
buildSteps.description: Position the storage drum upright on a level wooden dunnage pallet or concrete block platform at least 15 cm above ground. Site in a dark, cool cellar or insulated pantry between 10°C and 18°C. Affix a weatherproof label recording Date Filled, Source Water, Chemical Dose, and Expiration Date (6 to 12 months). Rotate annually.
buildSteps.warningNote: Never store near gasoline, motor oil, paint thinners, or pool chlorine tablets; volatile fumes permeate plastic drums over time.

history.event: Cistern Engineering in the Levant: Plastered cisterns lined with slaked lime and crushed pottery hydraulic mortar allow dryland civilizations to store seasonal rainfall.

Construction of the Basilica Cistern (Sunken Palace): Subterranean vault measuring 138 x 65 meters with 336 marble columns, holding 80,000 cubic meters of emergency water for Byzantine Constantinople.
Lincoln Chlorination Breakthrough: Alexander Houston implements permanent municipal chlorination following a typhoid epidemic, establishing the scientific foundation for chemical residual protection.
Deployment of the Water Recovery System (WRS) on ISS: Closed-loop regenerative storage, catalytic oxidation, and biocide stabilization (iodine/silver) recycling 93% of habitat moisture.

inventors.name: Alexander Cruickshank Houston
inventors.contribution: Pioneered the microbiological theory and dosing protocols for residual water chlorination and storage stabilization.

inventors.name: Karl Ziegler and Giulio Natta
inventors.contribution: Invented coordination catalysts enabling high-density polyethylene (HDPE) synthesis, creating modern food-grade chemical-resistant storage vessels.

impact: Eliminates post-disaster waterborne epidemic disease (cholera, dysentery, typhoid) by decoupling settlement hydration from fragile electrical municipal pumping. Provides the indispensable 72-hour to 90-day survival buffer required for community triage, disaster stabilization, and planetary habitat bootstrap.

warnings: Never store water containers directly on bare concrete; volatile hydrocarbon fumes migrate through polyethylene over time.
Never use containers previously holding fuel, solvents, engine oil, or pesticides; polymers permanently retain carcinogenic residues.
Scented, splash-less, or color-safe bleaches contain toxic sodium hydroxide and fragrance surfactants; use only 5-6% pure sodium hypochlorite.
Water without a disinfectant residual will develop bacterial biofilms within 72 hours even in hermetically sealed containers.
In planetary habitats and zero-g closed loops, stagnant storage creates anaerobic slime and sulfate-reducing bacteria capable of microbially-induced corrosion of titanium alloy conduits.
